source: Fiorineschi and Rotini (2023) Uses of the novelty metrics proposed by Shah et al.: what emerges from the literature? Design Science 9:e11
finding: Shah, Vargas-Hernandez and Smith (2003) define four ideation measures: quantity, quality, variety, novelty. Variety and quantity score a set; quality and novelty score single ideas. Novelty has an a priori form (judges compare to a reference universe) and an a posteriori form (rarity inside the same session).
numbers: A posteriori: S_ij = (T_ij - C_ij)/T_ij x 10, where T = number of solutions for attribute i at stage j and C = count of this solution. Overall novelty = sum over attributes (weight f_i) and stages (weight p_j) of S_ij.
limits: The a posteriori score is relative to the one idea set, so it cannot measure novelty against the world. Attributes and weights are chosen by the rater. Formula read from the review, not from the 2003 paper itself.
agent_relevance: Set-level counts like T and C map straight onto code: cluster the agent's candidates, count cluster sizes, score rarity. This is a cheap judge-free novelty and variety signal.

source: Fiorineschi and Rotini (2023) Uses of the novelty metrics proposed by Shah et al.: what emerges from the literature? Design Science 9:e11
finding: Almost none of the 739 papers citing Shah et al. 2003 use its novelty metric in original form. Most that do use the a posteriori form.
numbers: 739 citing papers (Scopus, March 2021); 686 retrievable; 61 used the original SVS metrics (about 9%); 72 used a modified version. Among the 61: 63.9% a posteriori, 8.2% a priori, 3.3% both, 24.6% did not say which.
limits: Covers citing papers only through March 2021. Authors deliberately did not name flawed papers.
agent_relevance: The field has no single validated standard. Our agent should log which metric it uses and not claim comparability with published numbers.

source: Fiorineschi and Rotini (2023) Uses of the novelty metrics proposed by Shah et al.: what emerges from the literature? Design Science 9:e11
finding: Reporting quality of studies that used the Shah metrics was poor: many gave no novelty concept, too little detail to repeat, and ran no inter-rater test.
numbers: 24.6% of the 61 original-form papers named no novelty concept (most common label 'unusualness, unexpectedness' 26.2%). Inter-rater agreement tests were rare, with no trend over the years. Most papers did not say how attributes and weights were chosen. All use found was academic; no industry use.
limits: Counts are of papers, not of effects. The authors read papers for method only.
agent_relevance: Any metric our agent trusts needs a stated rater and a check against a second rater. Plan a second-judge agreement test before any score drives a decision.

source: Fiorineschi and Rotini (2023) Uses of the novelty metrics proposed by Shah et al.: what emerges from the literature? Design Science 9:e11
finding: Known weaknesses of the a posteriori novelty score, as listed by the review from prior critiques: no historical novelty, can be too high even when similar solutions are common, and breaks when attributes are missing or extra.
numbers: Critiques named: Brown 2014 (subjective attributes, weights, stage separation); Srivathsavai 2010 (no link to existing products); Sluis-Thiescheffer 2016 (inflated scores); Vargas-Hernandez 2012 (boundary cases); Fiorineschi 2020/2021 (missing or extra attributes; refined metric proposed).
limits: Second-hand: this line reports what the review says. I did not open those primary papers.
agent_relevance: Define the attribute list once, up front, and freeze it. Re-scoring with a changed attribute list changes the score.

source: Fiorineschi and Rotini (2023), discussion section
finding: Reviewers should use at least two evaluators and report agreement. The two Shah novelty versions measure different things: a posteriori is psychological novelty, a priori is historical novelty.
numbers: The review calls the rarity of interrater tests 'a disappointing surprise'.
limits: Authors' recommendation, not an experimental result.
agent_relevance: Rule for our tests: two judges, one agreement number, one named novelty type.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review found LLM research ideas more novel than expert-human ideas.
numbers: 79 expert reviewers, 49 ideas per condition. Novelty mean: AI 5.64 (SD 1.76), AI + human rerank 5.81 (SD 1.66), human 4.84 (SD 1.79), p<0.01 (Welch, Bonferroni); 119 human-idea reviews, 109 per AI condition. Feasibility and effectiveness not significantly different.
limits: Ideas judged on paper, not executed. 7 NLP prompting topics only. Novelty is a rating, not Shah's rarity count.
agent_relevance: Novelty from an LLM can look strong before any test. Do not treat novelty alone as success.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Reviewers agreed with each other only a little above chance on research-idea quality, and LLM judges did worse.
numbers: Inter-reviewer balanced accuracy 56.1% (chance 50%). Reference: NeurIPS 2021 66.0%, ICLR 2024 71.9%. LLM judges: GPT-4o direct 50.0, GPT-4o pairwise 45.0, Claude-3.5 direct 51.7, Claude-3.5 pairwise 53.3, AI Scientist reviewer 43.3.
limits: Agreement metric is a top-vs-bottom 25% split-half, used because reviewers did not overlap.
agent_relevance: Both humans and LLM judges are noisy for idea quality. Do not let an LLM judge alone pick the winning idea.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Over-generating ideas hits a diversity wall: most new LLM ideas are repeats.
numbers: 4000 seed ideas per topic embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2; duplicate = cosine similarity above 0.8 to an earlier idea; only about 200 non-duplicate ideas out of 4000 (about 5%); the share of new non-duplicates kept falling.
limits: One model family, one embedding, one threshold (0.8 is a choice).
agent_relevance: Raw quantity is a poor metric. Use a duplicate-aware count (unique clusters) as the quantity measure.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
finding: Follow-up: ideas judged more novel before execution lost that edge after experts spent over 100 hours executing them.
numbers: 43 expert executors; N=19 human ideas, 24 AI ideas. Score drop of AI ideas relative to human ideas after execution: novelty 1.039 (p=0.025), excitement 1.835 (p=0.001), effectiveness 1.827 (p=0.003), overall 1.348 (p=0.004), FDR-adjusted. AI ideas scored below human after execution, e.g. excitement 3.90 vs 4.48, effectiveness 4.13 vs 4.78 (not significant at N=43).
limits: Small N; the ranking flip is not significant. NLP prompting ideas only.
agent_relevance: Pre-execution novelty is a weak predictor of outcome. Tie the agent's metric to a test result, not to a rating of the idea.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap
finding: Ideation-time scores barely predict execution-time scores.
numbers: Pearson r, ideation vs execution: AI ideas novelty -0.019, excitement -0.321, effectiveness 0.172, overall -0.092; human ideas novelty -0.084, excitement 0.205, effectiveness 0.022, overall 0.158.
limits: Per-idea N is 24 AI and 19 human, so every correlation is very imprecise.
agent_relevance: A judged score before running is nearly uninformative. Prefer measuring ideation by downstream test results.

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
finding: Study 1: GPT-4 product ideas had higher purchase intent than student ideas, especially in the top tail.
numbers: 400 ideas (200 human, 100 zero-shot GPT-4, 100 few-shot GPT-4). Mean purchase intent 40.4% human, 46.4% zero-shot, 49.3% few-shot. Zero-shot vs human B=0.059 (p<.001); few-shot vs human B=0.089 (p<.001). Top 10% (40 ideas): 5 human, 15 zero-shot, 20 few-shot.
limits: One domain (college students, products under $50); Prolific raters; GPT-4 March 2023.
agent_relevance: Quality can be raised by sampling many ideas and picking the top; the gain shows in the upper tail.

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
finding: Perceived novelty was lower for LLM ideas, and a style rewrite did not change quality scores.
numbers: Novelty: human 40.6% (SD 0.117), zero-shot 36.7% (SD 0.101), few-shot 36.1% (SD 0.11). Human vs zero-shot B=-0.038 (p=.008); vs few-shot B=-0.049 (p<.001). Rephrasing human ideas in LLM style: purchase intent B=0.009 (p=.205). Novelty vs purchase intent r(400)=-0.078 (p=.124).
limits: Novelty here is a rater scale, not Shah rarity.
agent_relevance: Quality and novelty can move in opposite directions. Track them separately.

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
finding: Set-level variety is lower for LLM ideas, across all five human-vs-AI datasets re-analysed.
numbers: Diversity = 1 - mean pairwise cosine similarity (USE embeddings). Gap human vs zero-shot GPT-4: B=0.193 (95% CI 0.182-0.204); few-shot B=0.207; 32 of 32 alternative-measure comparisons lower for AI. After style standardisation 80% (zero-shot) and 90% (few-shot) of the gap remains.
limits: Embeddings measure topic spread, not design merit.
agent_relevance: This is the modern replacement for Shah's variety metric and is cheap. Use it on the agent's own candidate pool.

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
finding: Diversity interventions ranked: varied personas and constraints, and pooling across vendors, get near human variety. Independent-session reruns and self-refinement do worse.
numbers: Diversity (1 - pairwise cosine): humans 0.773; random personas 0.757; human-picked problem agent 0.739; random constraints 0.735; GPT-4o chain-of-thought 0.698; random sonnets 0.686; GPT-4o zero-shot 0.679; GPT-4 zero-shot 0.585; refine-twice agent 0.575; GPT-4o independent sessions 0.452. Composite pool of four vendors approached human level.
limits: One task, one metric. Persona eccentricity was non-monotonic: the most eccentric prompts lost the gain (p<.001).
agent_relevance: Add diversity operators (distinct personas or constraints, different models). Self-refinement alone reduced variety.

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
finding: Scaling the number of AI ideas keeps closing the coverage gap but never fully closes it.
numbers: Mean nearest-neighbour distance from human ideas to the closest LLM idea fell from 0.546 (N=100) to 0.478 (N=1000); the max distance fell only from 0.762 to 0.711. Newer models (except o3-mini, fixated on desk organizers) were more diverse than March 2023 GPT-4; none matched humans alone.
limits: Coverage is defined relative to the human pool the authors collected.
agent_relevance: Coverage of a reference set is a usable second metric. Budget candidate count against falling returns.

source: Doshi and Hauser (2024) Generative artificial intelligence enhances creativity but reduces the diversity of novel content (Science Advances)
finding: Access to GenAI story ideas raised each story's rated novelty and usefulness but made stories more alike.
numbers: Preregistered; 500 writers, 293 stories, 600 evaluators, 3,519 ratings. Novelty +5.4% (b=0.207, p=0.021) with 1 AI idea and +8.1% (b=0.311, p<0.001) with 5; usefulness +3.7% and +9.0%. Similarity to other stories rose: 1 idea b=0.871 (p<0.001), 5 ideas b=0.718 (p=0.003). Low-creativity (low DAT) writers gained most: novelty +6.3% and +10.7%.
limits: Short stories; Prolific writers; one model; the AI idea pool was shared.
agent_relevance: Individual quality up and collective variety down is the core trade-off; any ideation metric must expose both.

source: Wan and Kalman (2025) Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation
finding: Modified replication of Doshi and Hauser: when AI ideas came from 10 diverse personas, the homogenisation effect was not found.
numbers: N=97 after exclusions (100 recruited). Story similarity: 1 plot b=-0.493 (p=0.301), 5 plots b=-0.356 (p=0.459); F(2,94)=0.573, p=0.57. Original: +0.871 and +0.718. Effect sizes d=0.47 (0 vs 1), 0.36 (0 vs 5), -0.18 (1 vs 5); post-hoc power 55.4%; about 165 total needed for 80%. Bayes factors 0.55, 1.72, 3.97.
limits: Underpowered. A null on similarity is not proof of equal diversity. Persona diversity was a deliberate change, so this is a conceptual not an exact replication.
agent_relevance: Where the AI ideas come from matters: a varied source can keep set variety. Supports persona-diverse candidate generation.

source: Anderson, Shah, Kreminski (2024) Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation
finding: Within-subject test: ChatGPT users produced more ideas, but the group's ideas were more alike.
numbers: 33 analysed of 36; 1271 ideas. Group-level similarity to centroid: ChatGPT M=.24 vs Oblique Strategies M=.28, t(32)=2.154, p=0.038, d=.47. Individual-level difference not found (p=0.352, d=.12). Fluency 8.39 vs 7.32 ideas, p=0.044, d=.32 (about +15%). Felt responsibility 48.17% vs 63.63%, p=0.003, d=.67.
limits: Small sample, recruited from university lists; ChatGPT 3.5; comparison tool is a card deck.
agent_relevance: Counts rise while set variety drops under the same intervention. Report count and variety side by side.

source: Ashkinaze et al. (2025) How AI Ideas Affect the Creativity, Diversity, and Evolution of Human Ideas
finding: Contradicts the homogenisation finding: seeing ChatGPT ideas raised collective diversity in a chained experiment, with no change in individual creativity.
numbers: 800+ participants, 40+ countries; Alternate Uses Task. Global diversity (median pairwise cosine distance, SBERT) higher with high exposure disclosed (beta=0.31, p=0.001) and undisclosed (beta=0.26, p=0.001) than control; low exposure smaller (about 0.11 in one cell). Control diversity fell across trials as people converged.
limits: Passive exposure, one simple divergent task. Differs from active use in Doshi and Hauser.
agent_relevance: The direction of the AI diversity effect depends on workflow: one shared source homogenises, one extra voice among varied ideas can diversify. Measure under the real workflow.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (CHI)
finding: Uses Shah-style fluency, variety and originality in a sketching task. Image-generator users fixated more on an example and produced fewer, less varied, less original ideas.
numbers: N=60 between participants, 20-minute sketching. Design fixation higher with GenAI (mean .32, 89% CI [.11,.55], Bayes factor 124); image search also higher (mean .27). Fluency total effect about -0.21 (89% CI wide, BF 3.2). Variety: GenAI 86% probability of a negative effect. Originality total effect mean -.03 (97% probability negative), described as negligible.
limits: Small N; Midjourney images, not an LLM; wide credible intervals, so variety and originality effects are not decisive.
agent_relevance: Fixation can be measured as the share of features copied from the first example. Our agent can log this against its first candidate.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) metric definitions
finding: Metric definitions used: fluency is sketch count; variety is clusters covered (normalised); originality is the share of other participants with no idea in that cluster. Two raters coded the sketches.
numbers: Originality = 1 - (other participants with ideas in the cluster)/(other participants).
limits: Rater agreement figure not extracted in my read, so reliability is unverified here.
agent_relevance: These are cheap programmatic cousins of Shah's metrics: clusters plus counts.

source: Egea et al. (2025) ChatGPT as an inventor: strengths and weaknesses of current LLMs against humans in engineering design
finding: In a 48-hour prototyping hackathon with graduate teams, the ChatGPT-4-led team came second of six. Concept generation was strong; fixation and early abandonment were weak.
numbers: 6 teams (5 human, 1 ChatGPT-led). Dart distance: winner 37.66 m, ChatGPT team 14.8 m (rank 2), average 12.0 m, others 8.07, 6.56, 5.06, 0.06 m. ChatGPT listed 5 working principles but only the 3 common ones were built; it dropped pneumatics after one iteration. 97 prompts coded into 108 codes.
limits: One run of one LLM, one task, N=1 AI team. URL given is the dataset DOI named in the paper; I read an author PDF copy.
agent_relevance: Real build outcome is the benchmark. Breadth of ideation did not mean depth of testing; add a rule to test the lead concept longer before dropping it.

source: Dong and Yakura (2026) Human diversity fuels collective creativity that large language models cannot simulate or sustain
finding: Preregistered metaphor experiment: AI-supplied ideas shrank the idea pool; AI used only to polish human ideas did not. LLM-simulated pools were less varied than every human pool.
numbers: 644 writers (318 native, 326 non-native English), 351 evaluators. AI ideation vs human-only: b=0.036 centroid similarity (p<0.001); AI refinement b=0.007 (p=0.516). Strongest simulation (Claude Sonnet 4.6) recovered 75.3% of human-only diversity; all simulated pools below all human pools (p<0.001). Higher temperature saturated below human level and gave degenerate text.
limits: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Metaphor task. Simulation not preregistered.
agent_relevance: Do not use LLM personas as a stand-in for varied people when you expect variety. Let the model refine, not originate, when set variety matters.

source: Dong and Yakura (2026), individual ratings
finding: Individual ratings rose with AI-supplied ideas even though the pool shrank: private benefit and collective cost point opposite ways.
numbers: AI ideation raised convergent creativity (aptness, explanation): L1 b=3.127 (p=0.007), L2 b=3.711 (p=0.001). Divergent creativity (novelty, surprise) rose for L1 only (b=4.753, p<0.001), not L2 (b=0.834, p=0.548).
limits: Preprint.
agent_relevance: A single-output score hides the set-level loss. Report both.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Beyond Brainstorming: What Drives High-Quality Scientific Ideas? Lessons from Multi-Agent Collaboration
finding: Multi-agent discussion beat solitary agent self-reflection for research proposals, but only with expertise and mixed backgrounds.
numbers: DeepSeek-V3 generators; 1000 AI proposals (50 seeds x 20 topics), 100 human-rated. Overall assessment +0.46 (Qwen3 judge) and +0.44 (o1-mini judge) over solitary. Human A/B on 40 pairs preferred multi-agent in 87.5% (p<0.01, binomial). Early-career-only agents OA 7.73 vs solitary 7.75. Diminishing returns beyond 3 agents or 8 rounds; longer discussion raised novelty but cut workability.
limits: LLM judges; human check only 40 samples (MAE below 0.5). No Shah-style rarity metric. One generator model.
agent_relevance: Cap cost: about three varied roles and five to eight rounds. Watch the novelty vs workability trade-off.

source: Sankar and Sen (2025) A Novel Mathematical Framework for Objective Characterization of Ideas
finding: Proposes an embedding-based, rater-free measure of idea-set diversity (UMAP, DBSCAN, PCA) as a replacement for rated novelty and variety, and shows existing LLM novelty raters disagree.
numbers: 30 expert designers (over 5 years) judged idea-pair similarity; dominant answers matched embedding cluster proximity except 2 cases. 40 graduate students each picked 10 of 100 ideas from cluster plots. Mean LLM-rater novelty: AIDE 3.83 (SD 0.31), CLAUS 3.43, GPT 3.32, SemDis 3.09, OCSAI 2.28 (SD 0.7).
limits: Authors' own method and validation; small expert panel; preprint v3.
agent_relevance: LLM raters of novelty disagree with each other. A cluster map of the candidate pool is a more repeatable base.

source: Kokate, Kompella, Onkar (2025) Leveraging LLMs for Design Ideation: An AI Tool to Assist Creativity (ALIA)
finding: Small pilot: groups using an LLM-run synectics-style prompting tool rated their own ideas better than control groups.
numbers: 6 groups of 2 (one of 3), about 30 minutes each; about 90% of participants had medium or high interaction with the tool; more of the tool group rated their ideas 'good'. No test statistic given.
limits: Self-rating only, no novelty or variety metric, tiny N, no inferential test. Weak evidence.
agent_relevance: Example of a study using self-rating instead of Shah's metrics. Do not cite as support.

source: Count across opened studies of the 'AI raises quality, lowers variety' claim (Doshi and Hauser 2024; Anderson 2024; Ashkinaze 2025; Terwiesch 2026; Wan and Kalman 2025; Dong and Yakura 2026)
finding: Replication status: lower set variety under AI in 4 of 6 designs read, null in 1 (persona-diverse source), reversed in 1 (passive exposure to AI examples).
numbers: Lower variety: Doshi and Hauser, Anderson, Terwiesch (5 datasets, 32 of 32 comparisons), Dong and Yakura. Null: Wan and Kalman (power 55%). Reversed: Ashkinaze (beta=0.31, diversity up).
limits: My own tally of papers I opened; not a formal meta-analysis. I found no peer-reviewed meta-analysis of this claim in this session. Web search budget ran out, so the search was incomplete.
agent_relevance: Build the agent so diversity is a designed property (varied sources, personas, models), not an assumed default.
